stages.journal: At Helstrom's landing, Okan-Zish, a rafter of the landing crew, told me a crocodile lairs in the shallows off the end of the crew's plank walk. It took one of their rafts, and no raft has gone out since. I'm to kill it.

The crocodile in the shallows off the end of the plank walk at Helstrom's landing is dead. I'm to tell Okan-Zish, the rafter of the landing crew who wanted it gone; he stands by the stone tower at the landing.

Okan-Zish owned that the beast was the crew's doing. Wuleen-Taza dumped fish offal off the end of the plank walk to scare traders off Sells-Dear's boat, and it drew a real crocodile; the crew's bait bucket still lies in the shallows there. I'm to fetch it for Sells-Dear, the boat captain, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.

I have the crew's bait bucket, still sour with offal. I'm to show it to Sells-Dear, the boat captain north of the landing by a house door on the west side of Helstrom's street, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet after all.
I showed Sells-Dear the crew's bait bucket. She kept it and paid me 60 gold, and with the rafters' trick known the river trade is hers.
Wuleen-Taza paid me 60 gold to keep the bait to myself. The crew keep their trade, and Sells-Dear still thinks the beast came up the river on its own.
Okan-Zish, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. Whatever the landing wanted of me ends with him.
Sells-Dear, the boat captain of Helstrom, is dead. Whatever the landing wanted of me ends with her.
Wuleen-Taza, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. Whatever the landing wanted of me ends with her.

objectives.text: Kill the crocodile off the end of the plank walk at Helstrom's landing.
Tell Okan-Zish at the landing's stone tower that the crocodile is dead.
Fetch the bait bucket from the shallows off the end of the plank walk for Sells-Dear, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.
Show the bait bucket to Sells-Dear, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.

lines: The Way to Ruins? North-east, a short way. You will see it.
You came back. Good. Sit on the bench with me, because my feet have had enough for today.
You there. If you want something hauled, say so. I have lines to pull.
There is a bench just east-north-east of here. An iron door just north-east leads indoors. The houses are a short way off, south-south-east and east-south-east.
The Panther River forks near Helstrom. I grew up on it, so I know it well.
You there. Haj-Wan wants an outsider to go after her kin Sei-Wan, who walked out into the basin alone. She waits at Helstrom's gate. I haul lines and nothing else, so I keep out of it.
I am Hauls-Wet-Rope. The dock bosses gave me that name and I kept it. I came down the Panther River for the work.
Namorine is just south of here. You will find him on the easy loads. Do not ask me to walk you there.
I haul the lines and the loads for whoever pays, here at the north end. A Dwemer ruin rises just south of here, so you cannot miss the place. Look at my hands if you doubt the work.
The Way to Ruins? North-east of here, passenger, a short way off, and you cannot miss it. If it is Gih-Xaleel you want, the levy warden, take the path south. He is a short way along it.
Well, look who has come back! Sit with me a while, my friend. I have been waiting by these ruins. You are better company than the water.
Passenger? Are you looking for a boat? I wait here for anyone who wants carrying along the water. Tell me where you are bound and I will tell you what it costs.

This is Helstrom, and I think it is the finest city there is. The Dwemer ruins rise just south of here, one beside the other. There are iron doors too, just south-west and just south-east, if you want to go indoors.
Many people call Helstrom the immortal capital of the Argonians. I say they are right. I have seen other places on my fares, and no other place compares.
Rumours? Helstrom and Stormhold have been rivals for a long time. I carried fares as far as the Stormhold side once. The people there haggled me down every time, so I do not go back.
I am Namorine, the boatman. I wait here by the ruins for a fare. My mother gave me this name and I have kept it, though the people of Helstrom cannot place it. Ask me about the water if you like.
Hauls-Wet-Rope works just north of here. She works too hard. Bejeen-Ul stands a short way south. I like his company.
If you need to sit, visitor, a bench stands just south-south-east of here. Sit on it and keep your weight off the old walls.

Climb south a short way, visitor, until you reach the waterfall on your left. Then walk south-west a fair way until you reach the bridge on your left. Follow the shore south-west a short way until you reach the old stone columns on your left, then follow the shore south a short way more. Helstrom is there.
Welcome, my friend. Sit with me by the stone for a while. I am glad of your company.
Visitor. Mind the wall. It is old, so do not lean on it.
A Dwemer ruin stands right beside us, just east-south-east. Another stands just north-north-east. Houses stand just west and just west-south-west, with an iron door just west.
Ask Namorine what they call Helstrom. I like her talk. I think the city is older than anyone's story of it.
Haj-Wan waits at Helstrom's gate, visitor. Her kin Sei-Wan went into the basin by himself. She asks for an outsider to follow him. I patch walls and cannot leave them, but I hope an outsider goes.
I am Bejeen-Ul. I patch the old stonework in these streets for the assembly's levy. The assembly pays me late. I like stone that does not crumble when I touch it.
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, keeps the gate a short way south of here. He is fair, visitor.
The alleys of Helstrom are counted both wonderful and dangerous, outlander. Keep your weapon sheathed in them and your eyes open.

Helstrom? Climb south-west, just until you reach the waterfall on your left. Then walk south-west a fair way, until you reach the bridge on your left. Follow the shore south-west a short way, until you reach the old stone columns on your left. Then follow the shore south a short way. Helstrom is there.
Way to Ruins? Follow the path north a short way, until you reach the old stone columns on your right. Then walk north-east a fair way. It is there.
Your face is known here and I have no complaint of you. The gate is quiet. Go through.
Outlander. State your business at this gate.
This is the gate of Helstrom, outlander. Dwemer ruins stand just south of me and just north-north-west. A stone tower stands just east-south-east.
A waterfall falls just south-west of here. Two bridges cross the water beside it, one just south-south-west and one just south-west. Do not wander far from the path.
Helstrom has never been taken by an army. After the Battle of Argonia the Empire never tried. The Imperial historians call our guard brutes. I do not care what they write.
I am Gih-Xaleel, a warden of Helstrom's levy. I keep this gate and I decide who goes in. Helstrom has never been taken, and I mean to see it stays so.
I sell nothing. I keep the gate. An iron door just north-north-west of here leads into a hall where a soldier of the levy stands guard.
Sells-Dear the boat captain is a short way west of here. Weesa-Nur is a short way west-south-west. Sells-Dear is sharp but honest.

Helstrom? Walk south-west a short way, and the bridge is on your left. Go on along the shore south-west a short way, and you reach the old stone columns on your left. Then keep to the shore south a short way more. Helstrom is there.
Gih-Xaleel keeps his post. Go along the shore north a short way. He is there.
You are back, my friend. I have counted every crate since you left. The count is better with you here. What do you carry today?
Newcomer. I count what comes off the boats. I also count who walks off with it. What do you carry, and how heavy is it?
Look at the old stone columns, just north-east of here. An iron door just south-south-east leads indoors, and a house stands just south-south-west. That is all I count in this spot.

Newcomer. A beast in the shallows took one of the landing crew, and no raft has gone out since. I count nothing off the rafts until one does. Okan-Zish of that crew is by the stone tower at the landing, and he wants it dealt with.
I am Counts-Every-Crate. I took a city name for city work. I was born in the interior. There a sack of food is worth more to me than a purse. How many sacks do you carry, newcomer?
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, keeps his post a short way north of here. He is exact. I respect that. Go to him if you need a man who keeps order.
I carry and count what is landed at the dock. It is just west-north-west of here. In the deep interior food, tools and safe passage are worth more than coin. I still think so.

Helstrom, walker. Go south-west, just as far as the bridge, and keep it on your left. Follow the shore on south-west a short way, until you reach the old stone columns on your left. Then keep to the shore south a short way more, and you are there.
Sit, my friend. The bench is long enough for two. The bridges are quiet.
Well, walker. What brings you to my bridges?
Two bridges, walker. One is just south-west, the other just south. The bench is just south-east. A house stands just east.
Taken? Helstrom has never been taken by an army. After the Battle of Argonia, the Empire never tried again.
I am a soldier of Helstrom's levy, walker. I came out of the marsh to serve. I will go back to it. Until then I watch the bridges from here.
Azum-Kai? He keeps watch at the stone tower, a short way south-west. He is keener than the post needs.
I watch who crosses the bridges, and how often. If you want boats instead, there is a dock just south-east.
Helstrom is close. Follow the shore south a short way, past the old stone columns, until you reach the boat on its rack on your left. Then follow the shore south-west, and Helstrom is just there.

The Dwarven Ruins lie beyond Helstrom. Follow the shore south a short way past the old stone columns until Helstrom is on your right. Go along the boards south-east a short way until the big ship is on your right. Then climb south-east over open ground a fair way until the standing stone is on your left. Follow the shore south-east a short way, and you will reach the ruins.
It is good to see you again, my friend. The watch has been quiet since you left. I have kept it carefully.
Halt, traveller. State your business at the stone tower.
Traveller. This is the levy watch. What brings you here?
A bridge crosses the water just north of here. South of here an iron door leads indoors. Old stone columns stand just south-west.
There is a bridge just north. The iron door just south leads indoors. I do not know what you want with it, traveller.
Helstrom's guard has a name for being dangerous. I know that name well. I mean to deserve one like it here.
I am a soldier and not a scholar of the province, traveller. I do know that Helstrom's guard has a name for being dangerous. The soldiers of the levy respect it.

Traveller, from this tower I watch the rafters sit idle. A beast in the shallows has taken one of their crew, and no raft has gone out since. Ask Okan-Zish, who stands near the tower here. He wants it dealt with.
I am Azum-Kai, a soldier of the levy. I keep the watch at this tower, and I take that duty seriously.
I took this post young. I keep the levy's watch here in full uniform. There is little else to say about me, traveller.
The two rafters work close by. Okan-Zish is just west-north-west of here and Wuleen-Taza just north-west. I do not trust either of them. I watch them closely.
I am a soldier of the levy. The stone tower stands just west-south-west of here, and I keep its watch. Benches flank it, just south-east of here and just west.
I serve the levy at the stone tower, just west-south-west of where we stand. Benches stand beside it, one just south-east of here and one just west.
Helstrom, dry-foot? I know that shore better than any boat captain. Follow the shore south a short way, and Helstrom is there.
Good, a face I know. Stay a while and watch the water with me, friend. Trade is slow, but the company is better.
Dry-foot. If you need a crossing, my raft is the best on this water. Nothing bigger is worth the trust.
This is the landing. I work it. An iron door just west-south-west of here leads indoors. Houses with doors stand just north-north-west and a short way north, past the bridge just north-north-east.
My people, the Agaceph, travel on thin rafts made for one, pushed along by the tail. I have never trusted anything bigger. For Helstrom and the Empire, ask Teeka-Xul.
I am Okan-Zish, an Agaceph rafter. I pole goods across this water with Wuleen-Taza, when the water is fit for it.
Wuleen-Taza is just east-north-east of here. I stand by that one in everything. Azum-Kai the soldier is just east-south-east. He watches us too closely.
There is a bench just south of here. Rest there if you must, customer.

Cross the bridge, just north-east of here. Then go north-east a short way, until the waterfall is on your left. Follow the path north a fair way, until the old stone columns are on your right. Go north-east a fair way from there, and you will reach the Way to Ruins.
Customer, I know you now. Sit with me a while. We can do business later.
Customer. What do you want?
A bridge crosses just north-east of here. The stone tower stands just south-south-east.
Ask Okan-Zish about the Agaceph and their rafts. He talks of them for free, customer. I do not give things away.
I am Wuleen-Taza, Agaceph, from the deep interior. I do the bargaining for the crew, because Okan-Zish is a poor bargainer.
Okan-Zish is just west-south-west of here. He is a fool. I look after him. Teeka-Xul the soldier sits a short way north-east. He is harmless.
Okan-Zish and I pole a raft on the water here. I do the bargaining. Ask Counts-Every-Crate about coin in the deep interior. I will weigh what you offer, customer, in coin or in kind.
The dock? Follow the shore south-east a short way. You cannot miss it. Mind where you put your feet on the way.
You again, my friend. Come in, but wipe your boots first. I will not have mud tracked through my house, not even by you.
Well. Look at the state of those boots. What do you want on my doorstep?
That is my door, just west of you. The house itself is just west-north-west. Keep off the step. There is a stone tower just south-west of here, and a Dwemer ruin just east.
Rumours? Ask Namorine about Helstrom and Stormhold. I hear plenty from my doorstep, but I do not give it away. The dock folk are thieves who sell it dear.
I keep this house. I have lived in Helstrom all my life. I sell what I can spare to the boats at the dock. Now, who are you?
Sells-Dear, the boat captain, stands just north-north-west of here. She ties up too close to my house.
I sell what I can spare to the boats at the dock. A bridge crosses a short way east of here, and the dock is a short way south-east. Count your change there, because the dock folk are all thieves.

Ruins, buyer? Climb east to the stone tower, it stands just there. Then follow the path north-east a short way, until the old stone columns are on your right. Walk north-east a fair way after that, and you are at Way to Ruins. I charge nothing for that walk. Hah.

The Dwarven Ruins will cost you good boots. Walk south a fair way, until the stone tower is on your right. Then follow the shore south a short way, until Helstrom is on your right. Then take the boards south a short way more, until the big ship is on your left. From there, ask again. The ruins lie further south-east. Hah.
Ah, I know that purse. For you the first price is the last price, friend. I will not even laugh while I say it.
Buyer! You look like you carry coin. Tell me what you need. I will tell you what it costs. Hah.
See the door close by, just west-north-west? That is a house, just north-west of here. A second door is just east. Hah.
A Dwemer ruin rises just north-north-east of here. Keep clear of it, buyer, unless you can pay for the trouble. Hah.
I am Sells-Dear. I run a boat out of Helstrom and I trade by it. I took a city name, because city buyers pay a city price to a city name. Hah.
Weesa-Nur lives just south-south-east of here. Be careful, buyer. She is a busybody who will count your coin before you do. Hah.
I trade by boat. Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza work the landing, a fair way south of here. They tell every customer I cheat them. I say they should buy a boat of their own. Hah.
Out in the deep interior food, tools and safe passage are worth more than coin. Remember that, buyer, when you are hungry and a boat is the only road. Hah.
Ask Gih-Xaleel about the alleys, and wipe your feet before you come in. I keep this floor clean.
You again. Come in out of the wet, friend. Mind the floor, though.
You. State your business, or move on.
This is the hall. The iron door opens on the street by the gate, just north-north-west of the warden's post. Stay inside if you have sense.
Helstrom has a name for being dangerous. The city has never been taken. I have heard worse tales than that.
Ask Namorine about Stormhold. I say the Stormhold folk are soft. I say it to anyone who asks.
Levy soldier. I guard this hall. I would sooner be indoors than on the street.
Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden. He keeps the gate, just outside that door. Go and see him.

take: Short, clear quest. A rafter asked me to kill a crocodile, then admitted the crew had caused it by dumping offal to scare traders off a rival boat. I exposed them to Sells-Dear with the bucket and got 60 gold. I understood the story and the people well, and the twist was fun. The choice between selling out and keeping quiet was a nice touch. Weak points: many lines show "[not yet written; the gist]" placeholders, the crocodile fight was a one-word win, and the world is very small. The ending leaves the rafters unpunished, and I would like to see what happens to them.
answers:
1. I'm not sure there is anything left. My last journal check was after reporting to Sells-Dear, and as far as I remember it showed no active objective. If anything is next, it would be seeing whether the rafters face consequences or whether Sells-Dear gives me more work. I would check the journal and look around once more, but I don't have a clear lead.

2. Nobody formally. I did the crocodile job for Okan-Zish, and then I took the evidence to Sells-Dear, the captain, because the crew had put people in danger and hurt a rival. He paid me 60 gold, so I am a freelancer who did a job for him, not someone on his payroll. I have no real loyalty to either side.

3. The "[not yet written; the gist]" placeholder lines were the most confusing. They broke the flow of conversations and I had to guess what was actually said. Next to that, the crocodile fight resolved as a single win/lose choice with nothing to do, so I had no sense of the danger. I also wasn't sure at first why Okan left out the bait detail that Wuleen-Taza gave me.

4. The setup is good: the crocodile hides a cover-up, and I get to choose between exposing it and keeping quiet. Fill in the placeholder dialogue, since it hurts the most. Give the ending some consequence, such as the rafters being punished or reacting to me, so the choice feels like it mattered. Make the fight and the world feel bigger. I'd also like a clearer signal of whether the quest chain is over or something follows.
